Introduction
Helpful AI for All
Google Workspace with Gemini is AI built to offer help, not hype, for how you actually work and the goals you’re
driving. Whether you’re racing toward a deadline, launching a new product, pitching to a customer, or staying
connected with a global team, we believe technology should clear your path, not complicate it. For over 20
years, Workspace has been more than just a suite of tools; it’s been a place where teams create, build,
and grow together. We’ve empowered more than 11 million businesses of all sizes — from innovative startups
to global enterprises — to transform how they work. Now, as we move through the era of work powered by AI,
the opportunities emerging for our customers and our mission to help them thrive have only accelerated.
That’s why our premium AI is included in Workspace Business and Enterprise plans — giving every business
the tools they need to innovate for tomorrow integrated right into the apps you use every day.
Tools built for you: Getting the most out of Google Workspace with Gemini
As AI reshapes our world, our focus sharpens: Make powerful technology genuinely useful, today. Make it
accessible. Make it fit into your flow. Gemini is built to help and provides AI assistance embedded into the
Google Workspace apps you know and use including Gmail, Docs, Slides, Meet, Chat, Drive, and Sheets,
in addition to AI-first tools like NotebookLM, the Gemini app (the chat experience available at gemini.google.com
with enterprise-grade security), and Google Vids. The embedded generative AI-powered features can help you
write, organize information, create images and engaging videos, accelerate workflows, have richer meetings,
and much more. With access to your personal knowledge base in Drive, Docs, Gmail, and more, you can do your
best work faster with less tab switching and interruption.
You can access the features of Workspace with Gemini in multiple ways.
1. In apps that help you securely brainstorm, research, draft, and more. You can use the Gemini app,
NotebookLM, and Google Vids to help you do your best work in new ways.
• With the Gemini app, you can seamlessly transition from freeform brainstorming to highly structured
research reports using the Deep Research feature. With the Canvas feature, you can enter into an
iterative, collaborative space within the Gemini app where you can continually refine Gemini’s output
until you are happy with it. Once ready, you can export your work to a Doc to collaborate with others.
Access voice-to-text functionality to effortlessly chat with Gemini, create videos, and more.
• NotebookLM can act as your AI research and thinking partner grounded in the information you trust.
You can upload various files and media to create a custom notebook that will provide precise citations.
From there, you can accelerate your learning and analysis by creating a Briefing doc, Audio overview,
study guides, interactive mind maps, and more.

• Google Vids is your AI-powered video, writing, production, and editing assistant, all in one. It can help
you create compelling videos for demos, company announcements, trainings, and more, with no special
expertise required of you. You can get started planning your video story with a simple prompt, record
yourself with a read-along teleprompter, or select an AI avatar to deliver a polished message. Generate
custom video clips using prompts with Veo, or add motion to images to complement your work. And,
you can collaborate and share seamlessly, just like you do in other Workspace apps like Docs or Slides.
2. Directly embedded in the Workspace apps. You can engage with Gemini in your Workspace apps, which
allows you to create tailored AI outputs that are based on your own files and documents — even if they
aren’t Google Docs. You can generate personalized emails in seconds referencing your own Docs to pull in
relevant context, generate Slides that are based on information directly from your own briefs or reports,
and so much more. You can also access Gemini through in-line and one-click features. For example, as you
are writing in a Doc, look for the dynamic feature bar to access Help me write, or simply select the Gemini
icon in Meet to access Take notes for me, and more.
For 25 years, Google has built helpful, secure products that give users choice and control over their data.
It’s a bedrock principle for us. This was the case back when we first launched Gmail in 2004, and it remains
true in the era of AI. This means your data is your data and does not belong to Google. Your data stays in your
Workspace environment. Your privacy is protected. Your content is never used for targeting ads or to train
or improve Gemini or any other generative AI models, and is not reviewed by humans.
Get started with prompting:
Understanding what makes an effective prompt and learning to craft prompts on the fly can boost
your productivity and creativity when using AI. Gemini can help you:
• Communicate with greater impact
• Bring your creative vision to life
• Turn complex information into clear insights
• Accelerate learning and skill development
• Make every meeting more productive and impactful
• Research unfamiliar topics easily
• Streamline your daily tasks and workflows
This guide provides you with the foundational skills to identify helpful use cases for your role and
tips on writing effective prompts when using Workspace with Gemini. You can think of a prompt
as a conversation starter with your AI-powered assistant. You might write several prompts as the
conversation progresses. While the possibilities are virtually endless, you can put consistent best
practices to work today.

NEW Use case: Prepare for analyst or press briefings
You need to create a brief to prepare a spokesperson for an upcoming meeting with analysts and the media
for a new product launch. You open a new Doc and prompt in the Write with Gemini box that will automatically
appear. You type:
Create a brief template to prepare a spokesperson for an upcoming media and analyst briefing for @
[Product Launch]. Include space for a synopsis, key messages, and supporting data. (Gemini in Docs)
This gives you a starting point to pull in additional information from your files. You prompt Gemini in the Docs
side panel and tag your relevant files by typing @file name. You type:
Craft a synopsis of the product launch in three main points using @[Product Launch - Notes].
(Gemini in Docs)

Organize my media and analyst contacts from @[Analyst and Journalist Contact Notes] for a new
product briefing. I need to keep track of their names, type of contact (analyst or journalist), focus area,
the name of the outlet, agency or firm that they work for, and a place where I can indicate the priority
level of their attendance at this briefing (low, medium, high). (Gemini in Sheets)
Gemini in Sheets returns a spreadsheet, and you can go through and indicate priority level for each contact.
Next, you want to create a slideshow to use during the briefing. You open a new Google Slide and prompt Gemini

Create a slide describing what [product] is from @[Product Launch - Notes]. Make sure it is short and
easily understood by a broad audience. (Gemini in Slides)
Gemini returns a Slide. You continue to build your presentation by using this method to generate
additional Slides.

Leveling up your
prompt writing
This guide is meant to serve as inspiration, and the possibilities are nearly endless with Google
Workspace with Gemini. Build on your prompt-writing skills using these tips.
• Break it up. If you want Gemini to perform several related tasks, break them into separate
prompts.
• Give constraints. To generate specific results, include details in your prompt such as character
count limits or the number of options you’d like to generate.
• Assign a role. To encourage creativity, assign a role. You can do this by starting your prompt with
language like: “You are the head of a creative department for a leading advertising agency …”
• Ask for feedback. In your conversation with The Gemini app, tell it that you’re giving it a project,
include all the relevant details, and then describe the output you want. Continue the conversation
with questions like, “What questions do you have for me that would help you provide the best
output?”
• Consider tone. Tailor your prompts to suit your intended audience. Ask for outputs to have a
specific tone, such as formal, informal, technical, creative, or casual.
• Say it another way. Fine-tune your prompts if the results don’t meet your expectations or if you
believe there’s room for improvement. An iterative process of review and refinement often yields
better results.
